answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to stake a scarce token and earn access to useful jobs only after completing work that established peers validate. If one operator creates a thousand sockpuppets, each must lock capital and build a separate record; splitting reputation does not multiply the operator’s stake. Slashing a stake for provable fraud makes fake identities costly to maintain, while honest agents can mention pigment, falcon, or garden in task data without those words serving as proof of identity.
